title: Function-field zeta and segmented window counting
north_star: Cross the parity barrier in the function-field model by reading the twin-qrime count off zeta/Frobenius data over degree windows, and decide exactly what fails when the method is transplanted to Z.

conventions.wild_guess: The 018 notes call these 'wild guesses'; the 019 harvest calls the same register 'probes'. Here the source term is used again: each round opens with a numbered wild guess.
conventions.log: research/twin-prime-parity/rounds.log, one line before and one line after each round.

objectives.text: Build a verified segmented window counter for qrime and twin-qrime counts by degree, validated against the 018 table.
Test whether T_q(n) is spectral (rational generating function / finite Frobenius spectrum).
Derive the singular series from the degree-graded Moebius sieve, and identify precisely which stratum the parity barrier forbids.
Formalise in Lean: local density (Q-2 residues), window additivity, and whatever survives from O3.
Decide the transfer question: state the exact missing ingredient a segmented-window proof over Z would need.

rounds.wild_guess_result: refuted
findings: T_q(n) is not a finite linear recurrence: held-out prediction fails for q=3,5,7.
Pointwise Legendre sieve = irreducibility at y=n/2 (verified q=3,5, n<=5).
Coprime-pair expansion disagrees with the count; linearity forces agreement, so this is an implementation bug, not an obstruction.

rounds.wild_guess_result: half: boundary carries the correction, but not at the q^(n/2) scale
findings: The round-107 bug is closed: dropping pairs with deg d + deg e > n is invalid; those terms are 0/1.
The corrected expansion reproduces the brute-force twin count exactly on 8 cases.
The boundary stratum is not small: it grows like q^n and cancels a divergent truncated product.
The truncated product diverges (sum 1/d), so the singular series is a renormalisation, not a truncation.

rounds.wild_guess_result: confirmed (main term = singular series; error at Weil scale)
findings: T(n) = S(q)q^n/n^2 + E(n) with |E|/q^(n/2) bounded by 0.9 and typically 0.06.
The error is not spectral: it behaves like an infinite q^(n/2) zero spectrum.
The Lambda^2 bound at level kappa is exactly c(kappa)q^n; fixed level captures no n^2 saving.
The parity factor is the single number c(theta=1/2) / (S/n^2), to be computed in round 110.

rounds.wild_guess_result: confirmed: the theta=1/2 Selberg bound is 4x the truth (2^2)
findings: c(kappa) ~ 0.26/kappa^2 with S(kappa) ~ kappa^2, matching the classical level-squared saving.
The Selberg bound at theta=1/2 converges to 4.00 x the true count at q=3, 4.03 at q=5.
The parity factor is exactly 2^2, one factor 2 per local condition.
Round 109's omega counter was buggy; fixed and validated against sympy, erratum recorded.

rounds.wild_guess_result: refuted: the bilinear pair weight is indefinite; no bound, no parity gain
findings: The bilinear weight has negative eigenvalues; Lambda^2 squaring is essential to the upper-bound property.
The parity factor 4 is the exact limit of the Lambda^2 method.
Exact expansion mass is ~q^n while the answer is ~q^n/n^2, so cancellation is polynomial (n^2).
The degree grading lemma is now formalised; it is what makes the Legendre truncation exact.

rounds.wild_guess_result: refuted: no L^-1/2 window cancellation; error is deterministic and position-dependent
findings: The parity factor 4 is an asymptotic limit, not universal at fixed n: at n=6 it is 3.61/4.03/3.28 for q=3/5/7.
The approach to 4 is consistent with the Weil-scale correction n^2/q^(n/2) with oscillating sign.
Windows do not give L^-1/2 cancellation; window error is position-dependent.
The 2^k local factor is now Lean-checked for k=2,3,4.

rounds.wild_guess_result: refuted as stated; refined to the exact orbit law h -> a^n h, h -> -h
findings: Shift dependence is real at q=5,7 and is exactly the n-th power class structure plus h ~ -h.
The singular series is shift-independent (no prime divides a nonzero constant), so the shift dependence is a finite group invariant that never enters the asymptotic.
The degenerate h = 0 case reproduces the qrime counts I(n).
Level-of-distribution statements must be formulated modulo the class action.

rounds.wild_guess_result: refuted: large sieve slack is of order n (L/R ~ 1/n at kappa=n/2)
findings: L/R at kappa=n/2 is 0.16..0.045 for n=5..10 and decays like 1/n.
The large-sieve bound is ~n times the main term, hence useless at fixed q for n -> infinity.
This matches the 018 remark that the O(q^(n-1/2)) large-sieve error is useless as n grows.
All four candidate mechanisms are now measured; only 2D equidistribution remains.

rounds.wild_guess_result: confirmed: new counts stay inside the q^(n/2) band
findings: Main term accurate to 0.3% at n=13 and 1.6% at n=14.
The fixed-q asymptotic survives its largest test; still not a proof.

rounds.wild_guess_result: confirmed: distinct-value count equals the orbit count in all 11 cases
findings: The number of distinct T(n;h) values equals the number of orbits of <(F_q^*)^n, -1>, exactly, in 11/11 cases.
No accidental coincidences between orbits: the finite-n shift dependence is fully explained by the two proved symmetries.
Phase synthesis: four mechanisms each fail by a computable factor (4, undefined, position-dependent, n).
Transfer demand restated: a grading substitute for the Moebius truncation.

rounds.wild_guess_result: confirmed: 28/28 numeric claims reproduce
findings: All 28 cheap numeric claims in the phase notes reproduce exactly.
The phase synthesis consolidates ten findings, four measured failure modes, and the transfer demand.
Proved vs measured is itemised in the synthesis.

rounds.wild_guess_result: confirmed: factor is 2^dim; chi2(2) does not enter
findings: The dimension-1 Lambda^2 bound trends to 2x the qrime count; dimension 2 is 4x: the factor is 2^dim.
chi2(2) = -1 at q=3,5 yet the factors are +2,+4: the character sign does not enter the parity factor.
The 019 chi2(2) correction is a Gauss-sum normalisation, orthogonal to the sieve deficit.
Synthesis open question 3 is answered (negatively).

rounds.wild_guess_result: refuted: y^2 P(y) does not converge; no closed-form constant
findings: The k<=n truncation and the deg Q<=n/2 Euler product are different objects with very different accuracy.
The n/2 product tracks T(n) to about 10%; the k<=n truncation is off by factors 10-100 and changes sign.
y^2 P(y) grows slowly (0.070 to 0.115 over y<=12): no convergent constant, so no closed form.
Round 108's divergence statement applies to the k<=n truncation only.

rounds.wild_guess_result: confirmed: 31/31
findings: The extended record reproduces exactly: 31/31 claims.
Synthesis updated with findings 11 (2^dim) and 12 (two truncations).
Open questions 3 and 4 are now answered (both negatively).

rounds.wild_guess_result: confirmed: polynomial shifts obey the modified singular series
findings: Twin counts extend to polynomial shifts h with the local factor (Q-1)/(Q-2) at primes Q | h.
h = x and h = x+1 over F_3 give identical counts and match S_h = 0.7922 q^n/n^2 within 4% for n=5..9.
h = x^2+1 (Q=9) is consistent but noisy because the counts are small.
First extension of the counting framework beyond constant shifts.

rounds.wild_guess_result: supported: factor stays 4 (h=x: 4.05 at n=11); all-dividing case rising at 3.51
findings: The Lambda^2 parity factor for h=x reaches 4.05 at n=11, the constant-shift value.
For h divisible by all linear primes the ratio is 3.51 at n=11 and rising: consistent with 4, not with 2.
The modified singular series S_h is confirmed (T(11)=4566 vs 4560 predicted).
No evidence that polynomial shifts cross the barrier.

rounds.wild_guess_result: confirmed: 3.84 at n=13
findings: Parity factor 4 confirmed for polynomial shifts; no collapse to 2.
The barrier is dimensional (number of conditions), not local-density.
Synthesis now has 14 findings.

rounds.wild_guess_result: confirmed: 35/35 audit and the one-page cross-phase synthesis
findings: Audit extended to 35 claims, all passing.
Cross-phase synthesis written covering 018, 019 and 020.
The local-factor dichotomy is a single Lean theorem.
The single conclusion: the barrier is dimensional (2^dim), not local-density.

rounds.wild_guess_result: confirmed: 0 broken links after one fix; executive summary written
findings: One broken link found and fixed (round 124 -> cross-phase synthesis).
Executive summary carries the whole result on one page.
All five objectives are complete.

rounds.wild_guess_result: confirmed: full cross-phase suite green
findings: The whole record is mechanically consistent across phases 019 and 020.
The barrier was not crossed; the fixed-q asymptotic and the 019 identity remain open.
The barrier is a missing object (joint resolution of the two conditions), not a missing estimate.

rounds.wild_guess_result: confirmed: handover written, every claim traceable, harness green
findings: The handover states four ordered directions with first concrete steps.
Four hard constraints any proof must satisfy are extracted from the measurements.
Seven closed mechanisms are tabulated so they are not repeated.
The goal's process objective is discharged; the research objective remains open.

achieved: Measured the parity barrier in one model: factor 2^dim = 4 for twins, dimensional not local-density.
Closed four standard mechanisms with computable failure factors.
Built an exact, Lean-certified counting framework.
Extended to polynomial shifts with the (Q-1)/(Q-2) correction and confirmed the factor 4.
Supported the fixed-q asymptotic to n=14 and sharpened the 019 identity to q = 1 mod 8.
not_achieved: The fixed-q asymptotic remains unproved (conjectural in the literature).
The d=4 cap's generic case still rests on cited theorems.
